name: Jasmine Miranda
life: “I still remember a necklace my mother could read upside down.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Jasmine by a small Tuesday habit. Jasmine takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I wanted the house number on a necklace so my mother can tell a driver where she lives.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a dark green knitted vest and a watch on a cracked leather band. Jasmine has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Jasmine steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: Jasmine finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To engrave a wearable address the mother approves.
family: Clyde Schmidt is Jasmine’s second cousin. Jasmine calls about good news first. Clyde is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A last ship together*, Clyde says, “I am the younger hand who gets the vacancy.”
connections: Marcel Lai. Scrap metal and an engraved address have two very different futures in the same workshop.
